story.title: Story 2: Event Capture and Turn Derivation

result.reviewScopeSummary: Initial verification of Story 2 against AC-2.1 through AC-2.8, TC-2.1 through TC-2.9, current capture source, capture tests, LHC intake behavior, health surfacing, and configured pi-lhc gates.

newFindings.title: No-id same-content events collide on idempotency keys
newFindings.evidence: AC-2.1 requires every finalized message to be recorded, AC-2.6 requires duplicate safety without dropping distinct events, and tech-design.md:329 requires fallback keys to be identical for the same logical re-delivery and distinct across different events using role/timestamp/content-hash. The implemented fallback in packages/pi-lhc/src/capture/idempotency.ts:38-60 uses fallbackId default "no-stable-id", blockIndex, role, kind, and content, with no timestamp or source-event ordinal. Production message routing in packages/pi-lhc/src/index.ts:348-357 may call mapMessage with only piSessionId when PI provides no entryId, and runtime-change routing in packages/pi-lhc/src/index.ts:362-373 always passes only piSessionId. Focused checks showed mapMessage for two no-entryId user prompts with the same text returns the same key, and mapModelSelect for two identical runtime changes returns the same key. LHC skips duplicate keys in packages/lhc/src/domains/intake-stream/internal/pipeline.ts:210-216, so later distinct events can be skipped.

newFindings.title: Unmappable PI hook input records no durable gap on writable threads
newFindings.evidence: AC-2.7 and TC-2.8 require a malformed or unmappable event on a writable thread to record a durable, queryable gap surfaced in health. The production hook path maps before capture: packages/pi-lhc/src/index.ts:348-357 calls mapMessage, then accumulator.onMessage, then capture. mapMessage has no default case at packages/pi-lhc/src/capture/map-message.ts:232-240; a focused check with role "bogus" returned undefined. That means onMessageEnd throws before capture can write a gap, and the generic guard at packages/pi-lhc/src/index.ts:385-400 converts the failure into a recordedGap:false diagnostic. The existing TC-2.8 test covers a malformed MessageEventInput passed directly to capture at packages/pi-lhc/test/capture/converter.test.ts:135-178, not an unmappable PI message through the real hook path.

newFindings.title: Multiple unsupported tool-result parts share one omission key
newFindings.evidence: Story risk reminder at 02-event-capture-and-turn-derivation.md:88-91 says unsupported image/file-reference parts must record an omission. mapToolResult iterates unsupported parts and emits one runtime_note per part at packages/pi-lhc/src/capture/map-message.ts:223-227, but each call includes the same toolCallId. eventKey then takes the toolCallId branch at packages/pi-lhc/src/capture/idempotency.ts:47-49 and ignores blockIndex/content, so two omission runtime_notes for the same tool result get the same key. A focused mapMessage check for a toolResult with fileRef a.bin and b.bin produced two runtime_note events with identical key `pi:thread-1:tool:call_1:runtime_note`; LHC's duplicate-key skip path at packages/lhc/src/domains/intake-stream/internal/pipeline.ts:210-216 means the later omission is not recorded.

verified: AC-2.1 / TC-2.1: covered for a user/assistant/toolResult sequence with assistant fan-out thinking -> text -> tool_call in packages/pi-lhc/test/capture/converter.test.ts:43-87.
AC-2.2 / TC-2.2: covered for the worked example; PI per-step turn_end hooks produce no LHC turn_end and agent_end emits one close in packages/pi-lhc/test/capture/turn-derivation.test.ts:39-83.
AC-2.2 / TC-2.3: covered for two runs each using turnIndex 0, ordered by source-event order in packages/pi-lhc/test/capture/turn-derivation.test.ts:86-118.
AC-2.3 / TC-2.4: covered for parallel tool results arriving b then a and correlated by toolCallId in packages/pi-lhc/test/capture/parallel-and-errors.test.ts:39-77.
AC-2.4 / TC-2.5: covered for isError tool results preserving error flag and content in packages/pi-lhc/test/capture/parallel-and-errors.test.ts:80-105.
AC-2.5 / TC-2.6: covered for graceful interrupt partial content, aborted disposition runtime_note, and closed turn in packages/pi-lhc/test/capture/abort.test.ts:29-65.

AC-2.6 / TC-2.7: covered for same-key re-delivery skip and normal resume no historical re-fire in packages/pi-lhc/test/capture/parallel-and-errors.test.ts:126-172 and packages/pi-lhc/test/capture/reattach-idempotency.test.ts:138-168.
AC-2.7 / TC-2.8: covered for malformed LHC intake event direct-to-capture gap and unavailable store health signal in packages/pi-lhc/test/capture/converter.test.ts:124-218.

AC-2.8 / TC-2.9: covered for a single model_select and thinking_level_select sequence producing ordered runtime_note events with new and previous values in packages/pi-lhc/test/capture/converter.test.ts:90-121.
unverified: AC-2.1 / AC-2.6: distinct no-entryId same-content messages are not safely recorded because fallback idempotency keys collide.
AC-2.8 / TC-2.9: repeated identical runtime changes are not safely recorded because runtime_note fallback keys collide.
AC-2.7 / TC-2.8: unmappable PI hook input on a writable thread is not proven to record a durable gap; code evidence shows it becomes a recordedGap:false diagnostic before capture writes anything.
Story risk reminder for unsupported image/file-reference omissions: multiple unsupported parts in one tool result are not safely recorded because omission runtime_notes share a key.

productionPathFindings: packages/pi-lhc/src/capture/idempotency.ts fallback keys can collide for distinct no-id messages and runtime changes, causing LHC duplicate-key skips in production capture.
packages/pi-lhc/src/index.ts handles unmappable PI message failures through the generic hook guard before capture can write a durable gap on a writable thread.
packages/pi-lhc/src/capture/map-message.ts emits duplicate idempotency keys for multiple unsupported tool-result omission runtime_notes under the same toolCallId.
additionalObservations: Configured story and epic gates both pass, so the blocking issues are coverage/behavior gaps not gate failures.
No material fake adapter, mock path, shim, or placeholder was found in the Story 2 capture production path; later-story NotImplemented modules remain out of Story 2 scope.
